findings.title: Draws 0 and 4 are attributed to die-row dents, but a slot1_free_end DRC coupling blocks their fix
findings.detail: §3.5 and §4 put draws 0 and 4 under 'die-row line moves' (dent plus fidelity), and the counts say 3 die-row misses (0, 4, 7) and 2 coupled-block misses. From b₀ and b₄, moving row_LS_u0 alone toward W*'s 11.0 mm is valid only down to 14.0 mm. Every value from 13.5 to 11.0 fails in_domain with 'slot1_free_end'. E0 and B4 work only because they also set slot1_u0 to W*'s value. The doc tests slot1_u0 only as an L2-sensitivity confound (B4b, B5), not as a constraint. The slot1 move needed to unblock the row is almost L1-flat (1.00783 to 1.00777 on b₀), so a strictly-improving search has no reason to take it first. So on draws 0 and 4 the binding obstacle beyond 14 mm is mechanism (b), a DRC-coupled move, not mechanism (a). The 'no DRC wall' in T3b holds only for a greedy path that moves slot1 first. The recommendation survives: option A's generic coupled-move retry covers slot1_free_end. From (14.0, 13.0) on b₄, paired −0.5 mm steps stay valid down to (11.0, 10.0), and L1 falls monotonically from 0.9987 to 0.9877. But the mechanism split, and with it the weight given to the 2 mm screen relative to the structured moves, is misstated.
findings.evidence: Checked with D.in_domain(spec, Params.from_vector(v), reach=True). b₀ (row_LS 14.5, slot1 13.0): 14.0 is ok (L1 1.0084); 13.5 to 11.0 return slot1_free_end. b₄ (row_LS 17.5, slot1 13.0): 17.0 to 14.0 are ok (L1 1.0093 to 0.9987); 13.5 to 11.0 return slot1_free_end. b₇ (slot1 7.5): the whole line to 11.0 is valid. The paired (row_LS, slot1) −0.5 mm path is valid on b₀ and b₄; its L1 on b₀ is non-monotone: 1.0084, 1.0078, 1.0084, 1.0074, …, 1.0059.
findings.suggested_check: Re-attribute draws 0 and 4 to the coupled (row_LS_u0, slot1_u0) block in §4. State in option A that its coupled retry must cover slot1_free_end on die-row line moves, not only on ±0.5 mm single moves.

findings.title: The claim that dents disappear at 2 mm is contradicted by the doc's own T5 data at draw 7's end point
findings.detail: The bottom line says the dents 'disappear at 2 mm and 1 mm mesh'. §6 says that at 2 mm 'L1 resolves the coordinate's sign'. §3.4 says the noise is '3–4 times smaller' at 2 mm. In t5_l1_mesh.json at 2 mm, the first step from b₇ toward W* still goes uphill (+0.00016), and so does the step away (1.0048 > 1.0028). So b₇ is still a strict local minimum along row_LS_u0 at 2 mm, with 3 slope sign changes. Draw 6 behaves the same way (+0.00053; 3 sign changes). The RMS falls only 2.1× on draw 7 and 2.3× on draw 6. Option A's 2 mm screen therefore does not by itself remove trap (a) on the one draw (7) that is a pure dent case. Option A's line moves would, because the 2 mm line minimum is at W*'s value. This weakens the stated reason for paying for the 2 mm screen: a re-derived W*, a re-aimed degradation target and a 6–9 h L1 stage. It does not invalidate option A.
findings.evidence: Recomputed from t5_l1_mesh.json. Draw 7 at 2 mm: 17.5 → 1.0048, 17.0 → 1.0028, 16.5 → 1.0030; first step +1.6e-4; sign changes 5/3/1 at 4/2/1 mm; RMS 0.077/0.037/0.022 %. Draw 6 at 2 mm: first step +5.3e-4; sign changes 3/3/1. At 2 mm the first step is improving on draws 4 and 1 (−9.8e-4, −3.8e-4).
findings.suggested_check: Add a 2 mm first-step column to the T5 table and qualify the bottom line: the 2 mm screen removes the dents on draws 4 and 1 but not on 7 or 6, where the line moves are what escape them.

findings.title: Draw 0's counterfactual is L1-improving only within the 4 mm screen's noise
findings.detail: The doc says the frozen 4 mm L1 rates every counterfactual as improving, so L1 and L2 agree on the direction. For E0 (draw 0) the L1 gain is only 0.19 points (1.0078 → 1.0059), and the path to it is non-monotone at 4 mm. That gain is at or below the doc's own noise figures (0.07–0.09 % RMS, dents up to 0.4 %). Agreement on draw 0 holds by point value but is not resolved. Draw 0 is also the closest miss (s 0.022), so whether a redesigned search fixes it is the least certain of the six.
findings.evidence: t4_l2_local.json: b₀ L1 1.0078, E0 L1 1.0059 at 4 mm and 1.0063 at 1 mm. My paired-step path is listed in the first finding.
findings.suggested_check: Report E0's L1 gain beside the screen-noise figure, and at 2 mm, in §3.5.

findings.title: The probability of proposing the coupled triple assumes equal steps; unequal steps are also valid
findings.detail: The ≈4e-7 estimate requires equal steps for (col_PHASE_u0, row_HS_u0, slot2_u1). From b₂ and b₃, (−0.5, −1, −0.5) and (−0.5, −1, −1) are also valid and L1-improving. The rule seems to be that row_HS must move at least as far as PHASE. So the estimate is a modest underestimate, but it stays of order 1e-6 and the conclusion does not change.
findings.evidence: in_domain and L1 from b₂: (−0.5, −1, −0.5) valid, 1.0104; (−0.5, −1, −1) valid, 1.0104; (−0.5, −0.5, −1) DRC fail. b₃ gives the same pattern.

independent_checks_performed: Ran the definition-of-done lint, `uv run ruff check research/o008_e011_diag`: passes. The deliverable file is absent from the review checkout by design: .mfos/policy.toml blinding removes research/diagnoses. I reviewed its text from the packet.

Recomputed every T4 ratio from the committed raw solve files (research/o008_e011_diag/l2/solves/em_lat0.5_<fp>.json) against the local W* solve. All 15 cases match the table, all are status ok with gmres flag 0, and local W* equals the burst to 7e-15. The 2.6–5.6 point drops and the 0.987–0.998 range follow from T1 and T4.

Refitted T2 myself with fingerprint-checked twin._l1 values and burst L2. At lat0.5 (n = 168) it reproduces a = 0.7105, c = 0.0131, sd 0.0164, r(residual, row_LS_u0) = 0.899 and +0.48 %/mm. New check at lat0.25 (51 layouts): a = 0.717, r = 0.82, +0.45 %/mm with row_LS_u0 in the fit. The die-row term is not an artifact of the 0.5 mm level, which partly answers the doc's own open §9 item.

Recomputed the T5 roughness metrics (quadratic-residual RMS, slope sign changes, first steps at 4/2/1 mm) from t5_l1_mesh.json. The 4 mm and 1 mm columns match. The 2 mm first steps show the draw-7 and draw-6 dents survive (finding 2).

Ran D.in_domain directly on the coupled triple from b₂ and b₃. Single and paired moves fail with 'slot2_free_end' as claimed, and the triple is valid with L1 1.0082 and 1.0383 as claimed. Some unequal-step variants are also valid (finding 4).
Read local._joint and LocalConfig (n_joint 12, k in 2..4, steps 1..4, uniform over 36 parameters). They are consistent with the doc's order-of-magnitude proposal probability.

Scanned row_LS_u0 alone toward W* from b₀, b₄ and b₇ with in_domain and L1. This found the slot1_free_end wall at 14.0 mm on draws 0 and 4 (finding 1). I also tested paired (row_LS_u0, slot1_u0) −0.5 mm steps: valid on both draws, monotone in L1 on draw 4, noisy on draw 0.
caveats: The root-cause conclusion holds within these limits: the search stops short of structured moves that both L1 and L2 rate as improving, H1′ and H3 are refuted, and L1 under-weights the die row at L2 (now also seen at 0.25 mm). The per-draw split by mechanism is wrong for draws 0 and 4, which are blocked by a slot1_free_end coupling, not only by dents. Coupled-DRC moves therefore account for at least 4 of the 6 misses (2, 3, 0, 4; draw 1 is mixed), not 2.

Option A's 2 mm screen is not shown to remove the dent at draw 7's end point. Along the die-row coordinates, the escape from the dents comes from the line moves. Read the case for the 2 mm screen as noise reduction (2–4×), not as removing the traps, when choosing between A and A′.
Option A's coupled-move rule must apply to the slot1_free_end binding that die-row line moves hit, not only to ±0.5 mm single moves. Otherwise draws 0 and 4 stay blocked at row_LS_u0 = 14.0 mm.

The counterfactuals are one or two moves chosen with knowledge of W*, not full searches. Draw 0's L1 improvement (0.19 points) is within the 4 mm screen's noise. The 0.25 mm confirmation of the counterfactual ratios was not run, by the doc's own statement.
I did not re-run the T3 path search, the T6 sensitivity solves or any new L2 solve. I checked only T1 and T6 numbers that bear on the findings above.
